-->

```{r, supp-setup}
sup <- tr("supplement")
fit_lab <- c(first = paste0(last_full, ", week 1"), final = paste0(last_full, ", final"))
col_fit <- c(first = col_ref, final = col_ink)
names(col_fit) <- fit_lab

# Parameter names as plotmath, for facet strips (label_parsed).
pm_lab <- c(
  hfa = "eta", b_prev = "beta", lambda = "lambda", kappa = "kappa",
  sigma_eff = "sigma[e]", sigma_m = "sigma[m]", nu = "nu", sigma_conf = "omega",
  `sigma_team[1]` = "tau[1]", `sigma_team[2]` = "tau[2]", `sigma_team[3]` = "tau[3]",
  `mu_tier[2]` = "m[2]", `mu_tier[3]` = "m[3]"
)
# ...and as LaTeX, for tables.
tex_lab <- c(labs, sigma_m = "$\\sigma_m$", nu = "$\\nu$")
tex_lab <- tex_lab[names(pm_lab)]
# ...and as bare symbols, for running text.
sym_lab <- c(hfa = "\\eta", b_prev = "\\beta", lambda = "\\lambda", kappa = "\\kappa",
             sigma_eff = "\\sigma_e", sigma_m = "\\sigma_m", nu = "\\nu", sigma_conf = "\\omega",
             `sigma_team[1]` = "\\tau_1", `sigma_team[2]` = "\\tau_2", `sigma_team[3]` = "\\tau_3",
             `mu_tier[2]` = "m_2", `mu_tier[3]` = "m_3")
sym_list <- function(v) {
  s <- paste0("$", sym_lab[v], "$")
  if (length(s) <= 1) return(s)
  paste(paste(s[-length(s)], collapse = ", "), "and", s[length(s)])
}

par_long <- function(fit) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(fit$par) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    pivot_longer(-c(.chain, .iteration, .draw), names_to = "variable") |>
    mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab))
}
chain_greys <- c("gray10", "gray35", "gray55", "gray75")
S_draws <- posterior::ndraws(sup$final$par)
n_chains <- posterior::nchains(sup$final$par)
```

# Appendix: Supplementary Posterior Checks {#sec-supp .appendix}

The weekly posteriors of @sec-computation are checked by gates and summaries only, because keeping every draw of `r n_snap` fits is not needed for publication. This appendix examines two posteriors in full, following the checklist of @kahleOverviewBayesianComputation2022 and @miyakawaPracticalComparisonBayesian2025 for applied Bayesian computation --- sampler behaviour; convergence (smooth, chain-consistent marginal densities, well-mixed traces, quickly damping autocorrelation, a Gelman--Rubin statistic approaching one); posterior geometry; the justification of informative priors and the priors they induce on derived quantities; sensitivity of the posterior to changes in the prior; predictive adequacy; and influence --- together with the visual workflow of @gabryVisualizationBayesianWorkflow2019. The two posteriors bracket the range the pipeline fits:

- **`r fit_lab[["first"]]`**: `r fmt(nrow(sup$first$played))` games, about one per team. The data barely constrain a team's strength, the hierarchy and the carry-over do most of the work, and this is where the hierarchical geometry is hardest for the sampler.
- **`r fit_lab[["final"]]`**: all `r fmt(nrow(sup$final$played))` games of the season, including the postseason.

Both are refitted with the production settings of @sec-gates (`r n_chains` chains, `r fmt(S_draws / n_chains)` post-warm-up draws each, `r fmt(S_draws)` in all) by the `supplement` target in `R/06_supplement.R`.

## Sampler Behaviour Across All Snapshots {#sec-supp-all}

Before the two detailed fits, @fig-supp-gates shows the gate statistics of every weekly posterior. The retry of @sec-gates is visible as the fits with doubled sampling.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-gates
#| fig-cap: "Gate statistics of all weekly posteriors by week, every season overlaid. Left: the largest rank-normalised $\\widehat R$ over all monitored parameters, with the gate at 1.01. Centre: the smallest bulk or tail effective sample size, with the gate at 400. Right: wall-clock time of the fit, four chains in parallel. Filled points are fits that needed the retry."
#| fig-scap: "Gate statistics of every weekly posterior"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.36
params |>
  transmute(week, retry = attempts > 1, `Max R-hat` = max_rhat,
            `Min ESS` = pmin(min_ess_bulk, min_ess_tail), `Seconds` = seconds) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`Max R-hat`, `Min ESS`, Seconds)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c("Max R-hat", "Min ESS", "Seconds"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, value)) +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(name = factor(c("Max R-hat", "Min ESS"), levels = c("Max R-hat", "Min ESS", "Seconds")),
                           g = c(cfg$gates$rhat, cfg$gates$ess)),
             aes(yintercept = g), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = retry), size = 1.2, colour = col_ink, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 19), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Week", y = NULL)
```

## Sampler Diagnostics {#sec-supp-sampler}

@tbl-supp-sampler reports the Hamiltonian Monte Carlo diagnostics of each chain [@betancourtConceptualIntroductionHamiltonian2017]: the adapted step size, the mean number of leapfrog steps per iteration, how often the trajectory hit the maximum tree depth (which would indicate a truncated, inefficient exploration), divergent transitions (which indicate curvature the integrator cannot follow and a potentially biased posterior), and the energy Bayesian fraction of missing information, E-BFMI [@betancourtDiagnosingSuboptimalCotangent2016].

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-sampler
#| tbl-cap: "Sampler diagnostics by chain. E-BFMI below 0.2 would indicate that the momentum resampling cannot move the chain across energy levels fast enough; the maximum tree depth is 10."
ebfmi <- function(E) sum(diff(E)^2) / sum((E - mean(E))^2)
sampler_tab <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble()
  tm <- fit$time$chains
  d |>
    group_by(Chain = .chain) |>
    summarise(`Step size` = fmt(mean(stepsize__), 3),
              `Leapfrog steps` = fmt(mean(n_leapfrog__), 1),
              `Max depth` = max(treedepth__),
              `At max depth` = sum(treedepth__ >= fit$metadata$max_treedepth),
              Divergent = sum(divergent__),
              `E-BFMI` = fmt(ebfmi(energy__), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(`Warm-up (s)` = fmt(tm$warmup, 1), `Sampling (s)` = fmt(tm$sampling, 1),
           Fit = ifelse(Chain == 1, fit_lab[[nm]], "")) |>
    select(Fit, Chain, everything())
})
sampler_tab |> ktab(align = "lrrrrrrrrr")
div_total <- sum(sampler_tab$Divergent)
maxdepth_total <- sum(sampler_tab$`At max depth`)
ebfmi_min <- min(as.numeric(sampler_tab$`E-BFMI`))
```

Neither fit has `r if (div_total == 0) "a single divergent transition" else paste(div_total, "divergent transitions")`, `r if (maxdepth_total == 0) "no iteration reaches" else paste(maxdepth_total, "iterations reach")` the maximum tree depth, and the smallest E-BFMI is `r fmt(ebfmi_min, 2)`, far above 0.2. The week-1 fit, with few data, needs no longer trajectories than the final one: the non-centred hierarchy keeps its geometry close to a product of normals.

@fig-supp-energy compares the marginal energy distribution with the distribution of energy changes between iterations. When the second is much narrower than the first, the sampler explores the energy levels of the posterior slowly and tails may be under-sampled; overlapping histograms are what a healthy fit looks like.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-energy
#| fig-cap: "Energy diagnostic. Grey: marginal energy $E$, centred; orange: the change in energy between successive iterations, $\\Delta E$. Pooled over chains."
#| fig-scap: "HMC energy diagnostic"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.34
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble() |>
    group_by(.chain) |>
    mutate(`E (centred)` = energy__ - mean(energy__), `Delta E` = c(NA, diff(energy__))) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(`E (centred)`, `Delta E`) |>
    pivot_longer(everything()) |>
    mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = name)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 60, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`E (centred)` = col_ref, `Delta E` = col_power)) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density")
```

## Convergence {#sec-supp-convergence}

@tbl-supp-conv gives posterior summaries and convergence diagnostics of the structural parameters: the rank-normalised split-$\widehat R$, which compares between- and within-chain variation after rank-normalising and folding the draws [@gelmanInferenceIterativeSimulation1992; @vehtariRankNormalizationFoldingLocalization2021]; bulk and tail effective sample sizes, which account for autocorrelation [@geyerPracticalMarkovChain1992]; and the Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior mean.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-conv
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior summaries and convergence diagnostics for the structural parameters. \\emph{MCSE} is the Monte Carlo standard error of the posterior mean."
conv <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::summarise_draws(
    fit$par, "mean", "sd",
    q5 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.05, names = FALSE), q95 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.95, names = FALSE),
    "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail", "mcse_mean"
  ) |> mutate(fit = nm)
})
conv |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(variable == names(pm_lab)[1], fit_lab[fit], ""),
         Parameter = tex_lab[variable],
         across(c(mean, sd, q5, q95), \(x) fmt(x, 2)),
         `$\\widehat R$` = fmt(rhat, 3), `ESS bulk` = fmt(ess_bulk), `ESS tail` = fmt(ess_tail),
         MCSE = fmt(mcse_mean, 3)) |>
  select(Fit, Parameter, Mean = mean, SD = sd, `5\\%` = q5, `95\\%` = q95,
         `$\\widehat R$`, `ESS bulk`, `ESS tail`, MCSE) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
worst <- conv |> slice_min(ess_bulk, n = 1)
```

Every structural $\widehat R$ is at most `r fmt(max(conv$rhat), 3)`, and the smallest bulk effective sample size is `r fmt(worst$ess_bulk)`, for `r sym_list(worst$variable)` in the `r tolower(sub(".*, ", "", fit_lab[[worst$fit]]))` fit. The conference spread $\omega$ mixes most slowly, as its autocorrelation in @fig-supp-acf shows: it is informed only by the forty-odd conference means, and its posterior is correlated with all of them. Monte Carlo standard errors are two orders of magnitude below the posterior standard deviations throughout.

The team strengths are too many to tabulate. @fig-supp-rhat-ess shows the distribution of their $\widehat R$ and of their bulk effective sample size as a fraction of the number of draws.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-rhat-ess
#| fig-cap: "Convergence of all team strengths $r_i$. Left: rank-normalised $\\widehat R$, with the gate at 1.01. Right: bulk effective sample size per draw; values above one are possible for anti-correlated chains, which NUTS often produces for well-identified parameters."
#| fig-scap: "Convergence of all team strengths"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.36
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  posterior::summarise_draws(fit$r, "rhat", "ess_bulk") |>
    transmute(`R-hat` = rhat, `Bulk ESS / draws` = ess_bulk / S_draws, fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  pivot_longer(-fit) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fill = fit)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(name = "R-hat", g = cfg$gates$rhat), aes(xintercept = g),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_fit) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Teams")
```

Trace plots (@fig-supp-trace-final, @fig-supp-trace-first) show the chains iteration by iteration; well-mixed chains overlap and look like stationary noise, with no trends, no stuck stretches and no chain wandering off on its own. Rank plots (@fig-supp-rank) are more sensitive: the draws of all chains are ranked together, and if the chains sample the same distribution each chain's ranks are uniform [@vehtariRankNormalizationFoldingLocalization2021]. Kernel density estimates of each chain's marginal (@fig-supp-dens-chain) should be smooth, unimodal where the model implies it, and indistinguishable between chains. Autocorrelation (@fig-supp-acf) should damp quickly with the lag, since it determines the effective sample size. Finally, the Gelman--Rubin shrink factor (@fig-supp-gr) should fall to 1 as the chains lengthen and stay there [@gelmanInferenceIterativeSimulation1992].

```{r}
trace_plot <- function(fit) {
  par_long(fit) |>
    ggplot(aes(.iteration, value, colour = factor(.chain))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.15, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = chain_greys, guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
    labs(x = "Iteration (post-warm-up)", y = NULL)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-trace-final
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Trace plots of the structural parameters, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". One shade of grey per chain.")'
#| fig-scap: "Trace plots, final fit"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
trace_plot(sup$final)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-trace-first
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Trace plots of the structural parameters, ", fit_lab[["first"]], ". With about one game per team several parameters are close to their priors, and the chains explore those priors freely.")'
#| fig-scap: "Trace plots, week-1 fit"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
trace_plot(sup$first)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-rank
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Rank plots of the structural parameters for both fits. For each parameter the draws of all chains are ranked jointly and each chain''s ranks are binned into 20 bins; the band is the central 95\\% range of a bin count under uniformity. Lines are chains; ", fit_lab[["first"]], " in orange, ", fit_lab[["final"]], " in grey.")'
#| fig-scap: "Rank plots"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
nb <- 20
per_bin <- S_draws / n_chains / nb
band <- qbinom(c(0.025, 0.975), S_draws / n_chains, 1 / nb)
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  par_long(fit) |>
    group_by(variable) |>
    mutate(bin = ceiling(rank(value, ties.method = "random") / (n() / nb))) |>
    count(variable, .chain, bin) |>
    mutate(fit = nm)
}) |>
  ggplot(aes(bin, n, group = interaction(.chain, fit), colour = fit)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = nb + 0.5, ymin = band[1], ymax = band[2], fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.3, direction = "mid", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = col_power, final = col_ink), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Rank bin", y = "Draws per bin")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-dens-chain
#| fig-cap: "Kernel density estimates of each structural parameter's marginal posterior, one line per chain. Orange: week 1; grey: final. Chains that agree give overlapping curves; a bumpy or multimodal curve, or one chain apart from the others, would indicate poor exploration."
#| fig-scap: "Chain-wise marginal posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
imap_dfr(sup, \(fit, nm) par_long(fit) |> mutate(fit = nm)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, group = interaction(.chain, fit), colour = fit)) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 0.3, adjust = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = col_power, final = col_ink), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free", ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-acf
#| fig-cap: "Autocorrelation of the structural parameters up to lag 20, averaged over chains. Orange: week 1; grey: final."
#| fig-scap: "Autocorrelation"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.8
acf_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  par_long(fit) |>
    group_by(variable, .chain) |>
    reframe(lag = 0:20, acf = as.numeric(stats::acf(value, lag.max = 20, plot = FALSE)$acf)) |>
    group_by(variable, lag) |>
    summarise(acf = mean(acf), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(fit = nm)
})
acf_df |>
  ggplot(aes(lag, acf, colour = fit)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) + geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(first = col_power, final = col_ink), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 5, labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = "Lag", y = "Autocorrelation")
# First lag at which the chain-averaged autocorrelation drops below 0.1
damp <- acf_df |>
  group_by(fit, variable) |>
  summarise(lag10 = suppressWarnings(min(lag[abs(acf) < 0.1])), .groups = "drop")
slow <- damp |> slice_max(lag10, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
slow_var <- names(pm_lab)[match(as.character(slow$variable), pm_lab)]
n_fast <- sum(damp$lag10 <= 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-gr
#| fig-cap: "Gelman--Rubin shrink factor (rank-normalised split-$\\widehat R$) of each structural parameter computed on the first $n$ post-warm-up iterations of every chain, as $n$ grows. The dashed line is the gate at 1.01."
#| fig-scap: "Gelman--Rubin shrink factor against iteration"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.45
gr_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  arr <- fit$par
  ns <- unique(round(seq(50, posterior::niterations(arr), length.out = 25)))
  map_dfr(ns, function(n) {
    sub_arr <- posterior::subset_draws(arr, iteration = seq_len(n))
    tibble(n = n, variable = posterior::variables(arr),
           rhat = map_dbl(posterior::variables(arr), \(v) posterior::rhat(posterior::extract_variable_array(sub_arr, v))))
  }) |> mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
})
gr_df |>
  ggplot(aes(n, rhat, group = variable)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cfg$gates$rhat, linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power) +
  geom_line(colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~fit) +
  labs(x = "Iterations per chain", y = expression(hat(R)))
gr_first_ok <- gr_df |> group_by(fit, n) |> summarise(m = max(rhat), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(fit) |> summarise(n_ok = min(n[m <= cfg$gates$rhat]), .groups = "drop")
```

The autocorrelation of `r n_fast` of the `r nrow(damp)` parameter--fit pairs drops below 0.1 within three lags; the slowest is `r sym_list(slow_var)` in the `r tolower(sub(".*, ", "", fit_lab[[slow$fit]]))` fit, which needs `r slow$lag10` lags, and even there the effective sample size is well above the gate. The shrink factors of every parameter are below the gate after `r fmt(max(gr_first_ok$n_ok))` iterations per chain in both fits and stay there, so the `r fmt(S_draws / n_chains)` iterations used are more than enough.

## Posterior Geometry {#sec-supp-geometry}

Hierarchical models have funnels: when a scale parameter such as $\omega$ or $\tau_1$ is small, the group effects it governs must be close to their mean, and the posterior narrows into a region the sampler can struggle to enter. The non-centred parameterisation of @eq-hier removes the funnel from the sampled coordinates when the data are weak [@papaspiliopoulosGeneralFrameworkParametrization2007]. @fig-supp-pairs plots each scale against a standardised effect it governs, in the sampled coordinates; divergent transitions, if any, would be drawn in orange and would typically concentrate at the neck of a funnel.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-pairs
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Posterior geometry in the sampled coordinates, 1,000 draws per panel. Each panel plots the log of a scale parameter against a standardised effect it governs: the conference effect $u_c$ of the first FBS conference against $\\log\\omega$, and the team effect $z_i$ of the FBS team with the fewest games against $\\log\\tau_1$. Divergent transitions would be orange.")'
#| fig-scap: "Posterior geometry of the hierarchical scales"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.62
geom_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  p <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$par) |> as_tibble()
  d <- posterior::as_draws_df(fit$diag) |> as_tibble()
  cr <- unclass(posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit$conf_raw))
  zz <- unclass(posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit$z))
  fbs_conf <- which(fit$conf_tier == 1L)[1]
  gp <- table(factor(c(fit$played$home, fit$played$away), levels = seq_len(nrow(fit$teams))))
  fbs_team <- which(fit$teams$tier == 1L)[which.min(gp[fit$teams$tier == 1L])]
  set.seed(1)
  keep <- sample.int(nrow(p), 1000)
  bind_rows(
    tibble(x = cr[keep, fbs_conf], y = log(p$sigma_conf[keep]), panel = "log(omega) ~ u[c]"),
    tibble(x = zz[keep, fbs_team], y = log(p$`sigma_team[1]`[keep]), panel = "log(tau[1]) ~ z[i]")
  ) |>
    mutate(div = rep(d$divergent__[keep], 2) == 1, fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
})
geom_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = div), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = col_ink, `TRUE` = col_power), guide = "none") +
  facet_grid(fit ~ panel, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(panel = label_parsed)) +
  labs(x = "Standardised effect", y = "Log scale")
```

Neither fit shows a funnel in the sampled coordinates: the standardised effects have the same spread at every value of the scale, which is the purpose of the non-centred parameterisation. In the final fit the team effect is nearly uncorrelated with $\tau_1$ and concentrated, because a full season pins the team down; in week 1 it spreads over its $\mathcal N(0, 1)$ prior, as it should with one game.

## Prior and Posterior {#sec-supp-prior}

@fig-supp-prior-post overlays the prior density of each structural parameter on its posterior in both fits. The comparison shows what the data teach: in week 1 many posteriors stay close to the prior, which is why the priors of @sec-priors were set empirically, while by the end of the season most have contracted well inside it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-prior-post
#| fig-cap: "Prior (dashed) and posterior densities of the structural parameters. Priors are normal, truncated to the parameter's support, except $\\nu \\sim \\mathrm{Gamma}(2, 0.1)$ on $\\nu > 1$."
#| fig-scap: "Prior and posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
prior_spec <- pri |>
  bind_rows(tibble(variable = "nu", mean = NA, sd = NA)) |>
  mutate(lower = case_when(variable %in% c("hfa", "mu_tier[2]", "mu_tier[3]", "kappa") ~ -Inf,
                           variable == "nu" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0),
         upper = ifelse(variable == "b_prev", 1, Inf))
post_long <- imap_dfr(sup, \(fit, nm) par_long(fit) |> mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]]))
rng <- post_long |> group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(value, 0.0005), hi = quantile(value, 0.9995), .groups = "drop")
prior_curves <- prior_spec |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab)) |>
  inner_join(rng, by = "variable") |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(variable = variable, {
    x <- seq(lo - 0.15 * (hi - lo), hi + 0.15 * (hi - lo), length.out = 300)
    dens <- if (is.na(mean)) ifelse(x > lower, dgamma(x, 2, 0.1) / pgamma(1, 2, 0.1, lower.tail = FALSE), 0) else
      ifelse(x > lower & x < upper, dnorm(x, mean, sd) / (pnorm(upper, mean, sd) - pnorm(lower, mean, sd)), 0)
    tibble(x = x, dens = dens)
  })
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = post_long, aes(value, fill = fit, colour = fit), alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.3, adjust = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = prior_curves, aes(x, dens), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_fit) + scale_colour_manual(values = col_fit) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free", ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density")
```

@fig-supp-contraction condenses the same comparison into two numbers per parameter [@schadPrincipledBayesianWorkflow2021]: the posterior contraction $1 - \Var_{\text{post}}/\Var_{\text{prior}}$, near one when the data dominate the prior, and the posterior $z$-score $(\E_{\text{post}} - \E_{\text{prior}})/\mathrm{sd}_{\text{post}}$, large in magnitude when the posterior sits far from where the prior expected it. Contraction near one with small $|z|$ is the ideal; high contraction with large $|z|$ indicates a prior--data conflict; low contraction indicates that the prior, not the data, is determining the answer.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-contraction
#| fig-cap: "Posterior contraction against posterior $z$-score for the structural parameters, for both fits. Prior moments are those of the truncated priors."
#| fig-scap: "Posterior contraction and z-scores"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
tn_moments <- function(m, s, a, b) {
  if (is.na(m)) {  # Gamma(2, 0.1) truncated to (1, Inf), by numerical integration
    k <- pgamma(1, 2, 0.1, lower.tail = FALSE)
    m1 <- integrate(\(x) x * dgamma(x, 2, 0.1), 1, Inf)$value / k
    m2 <- integrate(\(x) x^2 * dgamma(x, 2, 0.1), 1, Inf)$value / k
    return(c(m1, m2 - m1^2))
  }
  al <- (a - m) / s; be <- (b - m) / s
  Z <- pnorm(be) - pnorm(al)
  dal <- ifelse(is.finite(al), dnorm(al), 0); dbe <- ifelse(is.finite(be), dnorm(be), 0)
  aal <- ifelse(is.finite(al), al * dnorm(al), 0); bbe <- ifelse(is.finite(be), be * dnorm(be), 0)
  c(m + s * (dal - dbe) / Z, s^2 * (1 + (aal - bbe) / Z - ((dal - dbe) / Z)^2))
}
pmom <- prior_spec |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(pm = tn_moments(mean, sd, lower, upper)[1], pv = tn_moments(mean, sd, lower, upper)[2]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(variable, pm, pv)
contraction <- conv |>
  inner_join(pmom, by = "variable") |>
  mutate(contraction = 1 - sd^2 / pv, z = (mean - pm) / sd, fit = fit_lab[fit],
         lab = pm_lab[variable])
contraction |>
  ggplot(aes(contraction, z, colour = fit)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab), parse = TRUE, size = 2.8, seed = 1,
                           show.legend = FALSE, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_fit) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(NA, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Posterior contraction", y = "Posterior z-score")
```

```{r}
low_c <- contraction |> filter(fit == fit_lab[["first"]], contraction < 0.5)
hi_z <- contraction |> filter(abs(z) > 2)
final_ok <- contraction$variable[contraction$fit == fit_lab[["final"]] & contraction$contraction >= 0.5]
low_final <- setdiff(names(pm_lab), final_ok)
low_final_text <- if (length(low_final) == 0) {
  "By the end of the season every parameter contracts by more than half."
} else {
  paste0("By the end of the season every parameter except ", sym_list(low_final), " contracts by more than half.")
}
hi_z_text <- if (nrow(hi_z) == 0) {
  "No posterior lies more than two of its own standard deviations from its prior mean."
} else {
  paste0("Posteriors more than two of their own standard deviations from the prior mean are ",
         paste0("$", sym_lab[hi_z$variable], "$ (", tolower(sub(".*, ", "", hi_z$fit)),
                ", $z = ", fmt(hi_z$z, 1), "$)", collapse = "; "),
         ". These sit in the tail of their priors: not a failure of fit, but a sign that for that fit the prior is tighter than the data would choose. @sec-supp-perturb checks whether it matters for the published ratings.")
}
```

In week 1, `r nrow(low_c)` of `r length(pm_lab)` structural parameters contract by less than half --- `r sym_list(low_c$variable)` --- so their priors carry the fit, as intended in a week with one game per team. `r low_final_text` `r hi_z_text`

## Justification of the Informative Priors {#sec-supp-justify}

Informative priors need a justification that does not come from the data they are applied to. Ours come from the history of the sport. The structural parameters describe the game rather than any team --- how much a home field is worth, how noisy a margin is, how far FCS teams sit below FBS teams, how much of a team's strength carries over a summer --- and they should change little from year to year. `analysis/tune_priors.R` checks this directly: it refits the full-season posterior of every complete season, each with about 1,550 games, under the earlier, wider priors, whose influence at that sample size is small. @fig-supp-justify plots the resulting per-season posteriors against the priors now in use, and @tbl-supp-justify gives the numbers.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-justify
#| fig-cap: "Per-season full-season posteriors (points: mean; bars: $\\pm 2$ posterior sd) against the prior now in use (line: prior mean; bands: $\\pm 1$ and $\\pm 2$ prior sd). The priors are centred on the pooled mean and are at least twice as wide as the between-season spread."
#| fig-scap: "Per-season posteriors against the priors"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.95
pri_band <- pri |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_lab)) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab))
struct |>
  filter(variable %in% setdiff(names(pm_lab), "nu")) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab)) |>
  ggplot(aes(season, mean)) +
  geom_rect(data = pri_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = mean - 2 * sd, ymax = mean + 2 * sd),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = col_power, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_rect(data = pri_band, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = col_power, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_hline(data = pri_band, aes(yintercept = mean), colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean - 2 * sd, ymax = mean + 2 * sd), colour = col_ref, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1, colour = col_ink) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3, labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2015, 2020, 2025)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-justify
#| tbl-cap: "Empirical basis of the structural priors: the mean of the per-season full-season posterior means, their between-season standard deviation, the typical (median) within-season posterior sd, and the prior sd now in use. The last column is the ratio of the prior sd to the between-season sd."
pooled |>
  filter(variable %in% names(pm_lab)) |>
  inner_join(pri, by = "variable") |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab))) |>
  arrange(variable) |>
  transmute(Parameter = tex_lab[as.character(variable)], `Pooled mean` = fmt(pooled_mean, 2),
            `Between-season sd` = fmt(between_sd, 2), `Posterior sd` = fmt(typical_post_sd, 2),
            `Prior mean` = fmt(mean, 2), `Prior sd` = fmt(sd, 2), Ratio = fmt(sd / between_sd, 1)) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrrrr")
```

Three points qualify this justification. First, it uses every complete season, including the one being fitted, so it is empirical Bayes at the level of the sport; the prior sd of at least twice the between-season spread is the allowance for that, and @sec-supp-perturb measures what a different choice would do. Second, the earlier priors, set by judgement, were far from what the data support --- for example, an FCS offset centred at $-18$ points against a pooled estimate of $`r fmt(pooled$pooled_mean[pooled$variable == "mu_tier[2]"], 0)`$, and a conference spread centred at 9 points against `r fmt(pooled$pooled_mean[pooled$variable == "sigma_conf"], 1)` --- which is itself an argument for setting them from data. Third, the degrees of freedom $\nu$ keep the weakly informative $\mathrm{Gamma}(2, 0.1)$ prior of @juarezModelBasedClusteringNonGaussian2010, which puts most of its mass between about 3 and 50 and so lets the data choose between heavy and nearly normal tails.

## Induced Priors {#sec-supp-induced}

A prior on parameters induces a prior on everything computed from them, and a set of individually reasonable priors can combine into an unreasonable one. The quantities that matter here are not $\omega$ or $\tau_1$ but the spread of team strengths, the probability that the home team wins an even game, and the distribution of margins the model expects before seeing any game. @tbl-supp-induced simulates them from the priors alone, with the `r last_full` schedule and carry-over, and @fig-supp-induced compares the prior predictive distribution of three margin statistics with the values observed that season.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-induced
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Induced priors, by simulation from the priors alone (4,000 draws) on the ", last_full, " schedule, with the carry-over $d_i$ from ", last_full - 1, ". The last column gives the value observed in ", last_full, " where one exists.")'
ip <- tr("induced_prior")
ind_lab <- c(
  sigma_marg = "Marginal margin scale $\\bar\\sigma$ (pts)",
  r2 = "Share of margin variance from efficiency, $R^2$",
  nu = "Degrees of freedom $\\nu$",
  sd_fbs = "SD of FBS strengths (pts)",
  top_minus_12 = "Best minus 12th-best FBS team (pts)",
  p_home_even = "P(home win), evenly matched teams",
  p_top_vs_avg = "P(best FBS team beats an average one), neutral",
  sd_margin = "SD of regulation margin, all games (pts)",
  within7 = "Share of games within 7 points",
  home_win = "Home win rate, true home games"
)
ip$draws |>
  select(all_of(names(ind_lab))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), q50 = median(value), q95 = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(obs = ip$observed[name], name = factor(name, levels = names(ind_lab))) |>
  arrange(name) |>
  transmute(Quantity = ind_lab[as.character(name)], `5\\%` = fmt(q05, 2), Median = fmt(q50, 2),
            `95\\%` = fmt(q95, 2), Observed = ifelse(is.na(obs), "", fmt(obs, 2))) |>
  ktab(align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-induced
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Prior predictive distributions of three statistics of the ", last_full, " regulation margins, simulated from the priors alone; the vertical line is the observed value. The SD panel omits the ", pct(mean(ip$draws$sd_margin > 60), 1), " of draws above 60 points, all with $\\nu < 3$ (see text).")'
#| fig-scap: "Prior predictive checks"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.32
ip_lab <- c(sd_margin = "SD of margin", within7 = "Share within 7 pts", home_win = "Home win rate")
ip$draws |>
  select(all_of(names(ip_lab))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  filter(!(name == "sd_margin" & value > 60)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(ip_lab[name], levels = ip_lab)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = col_ref, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(name = factor(ip_lab, levels = ip_lab), obs = ip$observed[names(ip_lab)]),
             aes(xintercept = obs), colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Prior draws")
```

```{r}
ipq <- function(v, p) quantile(ip$draws[[v]], p, names = FALSE)
ip_in <- map_lgl(names(ip_lab), \(v) ip$observed[[v]] >= ipq(v, 0.025) & ip$observed[[v]] <= ipq(v, 0.975))
```

The induced priors are on the scale of the sport: before any game, the model expects the best FBS team to be about `r fmt(ipq("top_minus_12", 0.5), 0)` points better than the twelfth (90\% prior interval `r fmt(ipq("top_minus_12", 0.05), 0)`--`r fmt(ipq("top_minus_12", 0.95), 0)`), an even game to be won at home `r pct(ipq("p_home_even", 0.5))` of the time, and margins with a standard deviation of about `r fmt(ipq("sd_margin", 0.5), 0)` points. `r sum(ip_in)` of the three observed statistics lie inside the central 95\% of their prior predictive distribution`r if (!all(ip_in)) paste0("; the exception is the ", paste(tolower(ip_lab[!ip_in]), collapse = " and "), ", the statistic the fitted model also misses (@sec-ppc)") else ""`. Three induced quantities deserve care. The first is a warning. The $\mathrm{Gamma}(2, 0.1)$ prior on $\nu$ puts `r pct(mean(ip$draws$nu < 3), 1)` of its mass below 3, where the $t$ law has little or no variance, and those draws produce prior-predictive seasons with a margin standard deviation above 50 points (`r pct(mean(ip$draws$sd_margin > 50), 1)` of draws; 99th percentile `r fmt(ipq("sd_margin", 0.99), 0)`). This is harmless here, because $\nu$ is estimated between `r fmt(min(info$nu), 0)` and `r fmt(max(info$nu), 0)` in every season and its posterior contracts well (@fig-supp-contraction), but it is precisely the kind of implausible implication a prior on one parameter can have for an observable, and a prior bounded away from Cauchy tails (say $\nu > 3$) would be a defensible tightening. The spread of FBS strengths combines $\omega$, $\tau_1$ and $\beta d_i$, so a prior that looks modest for each piece can imply a wide or narrow league; the table shows it lands at a plausible `r fmt(ipq("sd_fbs", 0.5), 0)` points. And the prior on $\bar\sigma = (\sigma_m^2 + \kappa^2\sigma_e^2)^{1/2}$, which sets every win probability and therefore every $\pi_g$ in the resume, is induced by three separate priors; its 90\% prior interval, `r fmt(ipq("sigma_marg", 0.05), 1)`--`r fmt(ipq("sigma_marg", 0.95), 1)` points, is narrow, which is appropriate only because each of the three is well estimated in every season (@fig-supp-justify).

## Posterior Predictive Checks {#sec-supp-ppc}

@sec-ppc compared four summary statistics with their replicates. Here the whole distributions are compared (@fig-supp-dens), and then the location and spread of the margin within each kind of matchup (@fig-supp-stat-grouped), since a model that fits the pooled distribution can still misfit a subgroup, in particular the games across tiers.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-dens
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Observed distribution (black) against 50 replicated data sets (orange) for the ", fit_lab[["final"]], " fit. Left: regulation margin, home minus away, replicated from the marginal law of @eq-lik-marg and rounded. Right: efficiency margin, for games that have one.")'
#| fig-scap: "Posterior predictive densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.4
fin <- sup$final
he <- fin$played$has_eff
rep_long <- bind_rows(
  as_tibble(t(fin$yrep[1:50, ]), .name_repair = \(n) paste0("r", seq_along(n))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rep") |> mutate(signal = "Regulation margin"),
  as_tibble(t(fin$erep[1:50, he]), .name_repair = \(n) paste0("r", seq_along(n))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rep") |> mutate(signal = "Efficiency margin")
)
obs_long <- bind_rows(tibble(value = fin$played$margin, signal = "Regulation margin"),
                      tibble(value = fin$played$eff[he], signal = "Efficiency margin"))
ggplot() +
  geom_density(data = rep_long, aes(value, group = rep), colour = col_power, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.2, bw = 3) +
  geom_density(data = obs_long, aes(value), colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.7, bw = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~factor(signal, levels = c("Regulation margin", "Efficiency margin")), scales = "free") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-80, 80)) +
  labs(x = "Points, home minus away", y = "Density")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-stat-grouped
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Grouped test statistics, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". Histograms: the mean and standard deviation of the regulation margin over 100 replicated data sets, within each kind of matchup; vertical line: the observed value. The label gives the posterior predictive $p$-value, the share of replicates at least as large as the observed statistic.")'
#| fig-scap: "Grouped posterior predictive test statistics"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
tier_name <- c("FBS", "FCS", "Lower")
grp <- with(fin, {
  th <- teams$tier[played$home]; ta <- teams$tier[played$away]
  paste(tier_name[pmin(th, ta)], tier_name[pmax(th, ta)], sep = "--")
})
grp_keep <- names(which(table(grp) >= 30))
stat_rep <- map_dfr(grp_keep, function(gname) {
  idx <- grp == gname
  bind_rows(
    tibble(stat = "Mean", value = rowMeans(fin$yrep[, idx, drop = FALSE])),
    tibble(stat = "SD", value = apply(fin$yrep[, idx, drop = FALSE], 1, sd))
  ) |> mutate(group = paste0(gname, " (", sum(idx), ")"),
              obs = ifelse(stat == "Mean", mean(fin$played$margin[idx]), sd(fin$played$margin[idx])))
})
stat_p <- stat_rep |> group_by(group, stat) |>
  summarise(obs = first(obs), p = mean(value >= obs), .groups = "drop")
stat_rep |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = col_ref, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(data = stat_p, aes(xintercept = obs), colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = stat_p, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = paste0("p = ", fmt(p, 2))),
            hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.4, size = 2.7) +
  facet_wrap(stat ~ group, scales = "free", nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Replicates")
```

```{r}
stat_out <- stat_p |> filter(p < 0.025 | p > 0.975)
stat_out_text <- if (nrow(stat_out) == 0) {
  "none falls outside $(0.025, 0.975)$"
} else {
  paste0(nrow(stat_out), if (nrow(stat_out) == 1) " falls" else " fall", " outside $(0.025, 0.975)$: the ",
         paste(tolower(stat_out$stat), "in", sub(" [(].*", "", stat_out$group), "games", collapse = " and the "),
         ", where the observed value is ", ifelse(stat_out$p > 0.975, "smaller", "larger"),
         " than almost every replicate")
}
```

Across the `r nrow(stat_p)` grouped statistics the posterior predictive $p$-values run from `r fmt(min(stat_p$p), 2)` to `r fmt(max(stat_p$p), 2)`, and `r stat_out_text`. The tier offsets therefore place cross-tier games about right in location, and the misfit of @sec-ppc is mainly one of shape. Games across tiers are, if anything, less variable than a single margin scale for all games allows: a tier-specific scale is a natural refinement. The density overlay shows the same shape misfit directly: the observed margin has a sharper peak near zero than any replicate.

The leave-one-out probability integral transform (LOO-PIT) checks calibration game by game without using a game to predict itself: for each game, $\Pr(y_g^{\text{rep}} \le y_g \mid \text{all other games})$, estimated with the Pareto-smoothed importance weights of the LOO computation. If the model is calibrated these values are uniform; a U shape indicates predictive distributions that are too narrow, a hump that they are too wide [@gabryVisualizationBayesianWorkflow2019; @sailynojaGraphicalTestDiscrete2022]. @fig-supp-pit shows them for both signals and both fits.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-pit
#| fig-cap: "LOO-PIT histograms, 20 bins; the band is the central 95\\% range of a bin count under uniformity. Margins are whole numbers while the model is continuous, which spreads each PIT value over an interval of width about $1/\\bar\\sigma \\approx 0.08$ and does not by itself cause non-uniformity at this bin width."
#| fig-scap: "LOO-PIT histograms"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.6
pit_df <- imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  bind_rows(tibble(pit = fit$pit_margin, signal = "Regulation margin"),
            tibble(pit = fit$pit_eff, signal = "Efficiency margin")) |>
    filter(!is.na(pit)) |> mutate(fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  mutate(signal = factor(signal, levels = c("Regulation margin", "Efficiency margin")))
pit_band <- pit_df |> count(fit, signal) |>
  mutate(lo = qbinom(0.025, n, 1 / 20) / (n / 20), hi = qbinom(0.975, n, 1 / 20) / (n / 20))
pit_df |>
  ggplot(aes(pit)) +
  geom_rect(data = pit_band, aes(xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = col_faint, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.05),
                 fill = col_power, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = col_ink, linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(signal ~ fit) +
  labs(x = "LOO-PIT", y = "Density")
```

```{r}
pit_out <- pit_df |>
  mutate(bin = pmin(floor(pit * 20) + 1, 20)) |>
  count(fit, signal, bin) |>
  left_join(pit_df |> count(fit, signal, name = "N"), by = c("fit", "signal")) |>
  mutate(out = n < qbinom(0.025, N, 0.05) | n > qbinom(0.975, N, 0.05)) |>
  summarise(out = sum(out), bins = n())
```

Of the `r pit_out$bins` histogram bins across the four panels, `r pit_out$out` fall outside their 95\% band, against about `r fmt(0.05 * pit_out$bins, 0)` expected by chance. There is no U shape or hump, so the predictive distributions are neither systematically too narrow nor too wide, in week 1 or at the end of the season.

@fig-supp-resid plots the observed margin minus its posterior mean against that mean. A systematic trend would mean that the model's spreads are biased for lopsided or for close matchups --- for example, if strong favourites won by less than predicted.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-resid
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Residual regulation margin against the posterior mean margin, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". The line is a LOESS smooth with a 95\\% band; points are games, by kind of matchup.")'
#| fig-scap: "Residuals against predicted margin"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.5
tibble(mu = fin$mu_mean, resid = fin$played$margin - fin$mu_mean,
       group = ifelse(grp == "FBS--FBS", "FBS--FBS", "Other")) |>
  ggplot(aes(mu, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group), size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = col_power, fill = col_power, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FBS--FBS` = col_ink, Other = col_ref)) +
  labs(x = "Posterior mean margin (points)", y = "Observed minus mean (points)")
```

## Influence and PSIS Diagnostics {#sec-supp-loo}

The Pareto $\hat k$ of each game estimates the tail shape of its importance ratios in PSIS-LOO; values above 0.7 mean the leave-one-out approximation is unreliable for that game, and in practice that the game is highly influential on the posterior [@vehtariParetoSmoothedImportance2024]. @fig-supp-khat plots every game's $\hat k$ in both fits, and @tbl-supp-khat lists the games above 0.7 in the final fit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-khat
#| fig-cap: "Pareto $\\hat k$ for each game, in schedule order. Dashed lines at 0.5 and 0.7."
#| fig-scap: "Pareto k diagnostics"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.4
imap_dfr(sup, function(fit, nm) {
  tibble(game = seq_along(fit$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k), k = fit$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k,
         cross = fit$teams$tier[fit$played$home] != fit$teams$tier[fit$played$away],
         fit = fit_lab[[nm]])
}) |>
  ggplot(aes(game, k)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.5, 0.7), linetype = "dashed", colour = col_power, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = cross), size = 0.7, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = col_ref, `TRUE` = col_ink),
                      labels = c(`FALSE` = "Same tier", `TRUE` = "Across tiers")) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Game", y = expression(hat(k)))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-khat
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Games with Pareto $\\hat k > 0.7$ in the ", fit_lab[["final"]], " fit, largest first. \\emph{Games} counts each team''s games in the fit.")'
gp <- table(factor(c(fin$played$home, fin$played$away), levels = seq_len(nrow(fin$teams))))
esc <- \(x) gsub("&", "\\&", x, fixed = TRUE)
khat_tab <- tibble(k = fin$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k, h = fin$played$home, a = fin$played$away,
                   hp = fin$played$home_points, ap = fin$played$away_points, wk = fin$played$week_seq) |>
  filter(k > 0.7) |>
  arrange(desc(k))
if (nrow(khat_tab) > 0) {
  khat_tab |>
    transmute(Week = wk,
              Home = sprintf("%s (%s, %d)", esc(fin$teams$team[h]), tier_name[fin$teams$tier[h]], gp[h]),
              Away = sprintf("%s (%s, %d)", esc(fin$teams$team[a]), tier_name[fin$teams$tier[a]], gp[a]),
              Score = paste0(hp, "--", ap), `$\\hat k$` = fmt(k, 2)) |>
    rename(`Home (tier, games)` = Home, `Away (tier, games)` = Away) |>
    ktab(align = "rllrr")
}
```

```{r}
k_first <- sum(sup$first$loo$diagnostics$pareto_k > 0.7)
k_final <- nrow(khat_tab)
```

`r k_final` of `r fmt(nrow(fin$played))` games exceed 0.7 in the final fit and `r k_first` of `r fmt(nrow(sup$first$played))` in week 1. In the final fit every such game is an FCS team's only game against a lower-division opponent: that game is the only evidence about the lower-division team, so removing it changes that team's posterior completely. None involves an FBS team, and the estimated expected log predictive density is not materially affected. A $K$-fold refit would remove the approximation for these games if it were needed.

## Power-scaling Sensitivity {#sec-supp-powerscale}

@tbl-sens summarised power-scaling sensitivity by a single distance per parameter. @fig-supp-powerscale shows what lies behind it for the parameters flagged most often: the posterior density as the prior (top row) or the likelihood (bottom row) is raised to powers between 0.8 and 1.25 [@kallioinenDetectingDiagnosingPrior2024]. A density that shifts with the prior power is prior-sensitive; one that shifts with the likelihood power is informed by the data.

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-powerscale
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Power-scaled posterior densities, ", fit_lab[["final"]], ". Darker lines are larger powers $\\alpha$; the base posterior is $\\alpha = 1$.")'
#| fig-scap: "Power-scaled posterior densities"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.55
ps <- fin$powerscale
flag_vars <- c("b_prev", "nu", "mu_tier[2]", "mu_tier[3]", "sigma_team[3]")
if (!is.null(ps)) {
  get_side <- function(side_list, side) {
    map_dfr(side_list, function(d) {
      a <- attr(d, "powerscaling")$alpha
      posterior::as_draws_df(d) |> as_tibble() |>
        select(any_of(flag_vars), any_of(".log_weight")) |>
        mutate(alpha = a)
    }) |> mutate(side = side)
  }
  base <- posterior::as_draws_df(ps$base_draws) |> as_tibble() |> select(any_of(flag_vars)) |>
    mutate(alpha = 1)
  sides <- bind_rows(
    get_side(c(ps$prior_scaled$draws_sequence), "Prior scaled"),
    get_side(c(ps$likelihood_scaled$draws_sequence), "Likelihood scaled")
  )
  sides <- bind_rows(sides, mutate(base, side = "Prior scaled"), mutate(base, side = "Likelihood scaled"))
  if (!".log_weight" %in% names(sides)) sides$.log_weight <- 0
  sides |>
    mutate(.log_weight = coalesce(.log_weight, 0)) |>
    group_by(side, alpha) |>
    mutate(w = exp(.log_weight - max(.log_weight)), w = w / sum(w)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    pivot_longer(any_of(flag_vars), names_to = "variable") |>
    mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(pm_lab), labels = pm_lab),
           side = factor(side, levels = c("Prior scaled", "Likelihood scaled"),
                         labels = c("Prior~scaled", "Likelihood~scaled"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(value, weight = w, group = alpha, colour = alpha)) +
    geom_density(linewidth = 0.35, adjust = 1.3) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = "gray80", high = col_power, name = expression(alpha)) +
    facet_wrap(side ~ variable, scales = "free", nrow = 2, labeller = label_parsed) +
    scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Density") +
    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text())
}
```

## Sensitivity to the Prior: Perturbation Refits {#sec-supp-perturb}

Power-scaling is a local check: it asks what happens under small multiplicative changes to the prior. The requirement that matters in practice is global --- that a reasonable analyst with a different prior would publish essentially the same ratings. We therefore refit both posteriors under four alternative priors for every structural parameter: all prior standard deviations doubled, all multiplied by five (close to vague on the scale of these parameters), and all prior means moved up, or down, by one prior standard deviation. The last two move every mean at once in the same direction, a deliberately harsh test. @tbl-supp-perturb-par gives the structural posteriors and @tbl-supp-perturb-out compares what is published: the FBS power ratings and the resume.

```{r}
ps_all <- tr("prior_sensitivity")
sc_levels <- c("Baseline", "SD x 2", "SD x 5", "Means + 1 SD", "Means - 1 SD")
sc_tex <- c(Baseline = "Baseline", `SD x 2` = "SD $\\times$ 2", `SD x 5` = "SD $\\times$ 5",
            `Means + 1 SD` = "Means $+$1 SD", `Means - 1 SD` = "Means $-$1 SD")
ps_par <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) mutate(x$par, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
ps_rat <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) mutate(x$ratings, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
ps_health <- map_dfr(ps_all, \(x) mutate(x$health, fit = x$fit, scenario = x$scenario))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-perturb-par
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior means (posterior sd) of selected structural parameters under each prior. \\emph{Gates} reports whether the refit passed the convergence gates of @sec-gates."
show_vars <- c("hfa", "b_prev", "sigma_m", "kappa", "sigma_conf", "mu_tier[2]")
ps_par |>
  filter(variable %in% show_vars) |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%s {\\scriptsize(%s)}", fmt(mean, 2), fmt(sd, 2)),
         variable = factor(variable, levels = show_vars)) |>
  select(fit, scenario, variable, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = cell) |>
  left_join(ps_health |> select(fit, scenario, passed), by = c("fit", "scenario")) |>
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_levels)) |>
  arrange(fit, scenario) |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(scenario == "Baseline", sub(paste0(last_full, ", "), "", fit_lab[as.character(fit)]), ""),
         Prior = sc_tex[as.character(scenario)], Gates = ifelse(passed, "pass", "fail")) |>
  select(Fit, Prior, all_of(show_vars), Gates) |>
  rename_with(\(v) paste0("$", sym_lab[v], "$"), all_of(show_vars)) |>
  ktab(align = paste0("ll", strrep("r", length(show_vars)), "l"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-supp-perturb-out
#| tbl-cap: "Effect of the prior on the published FBS products, relative to the baseline prior. Power: Spearman correlation of the ratings, and the mean and largest absolute change in a team's rating (points). Resume: Spearman correlation of $\\WAB$, the largest change in resume rank among the baseline top 25, and the number of teams whose membership of the top 12 changes."
base <- ps_rat |> filter(scenario == "Baseline", tier == 1) |>
  select(fit, team_id, power0 = power, wab0 = wab, rr0 = resume_rank)
perturb_out <- ps_rat |>
  filter(scenario != "Baseline", tier == 1) |>
  inner_join(base, by = c("fit", "team_id")) |>
  group_by(fit, scenario) |>
  summarise(
    rho_power = cor(power, power0, method = "spearman"),
    mad_power = mean(abs(power - power0)), max_power = max(abs(power - power0)),
    rho_wab = cor(wab, wab0, method = "spearman"),
    max_rank = max(abs(resume_rank - rr0)[rr0 <= 25]),
    top12 = sum(xor(resume_rank <= 12, rr0 <= 12)) / 2,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = c("first", "final")), scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_levels)) |>
  arrange(fit, scenario)
perturb_out |>
  mutate(Fit = ifelse(scenario == "SD x 2", sub(paste0(last_full, ", "), "", fit_lab[as.character(fit)]), ""),
         Prior = sc_tex[as.character(scenario)]) |>
  transmute(Fit, Prior, `$\\rho$ power` = fmt(rho_power, 3), `Mean $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(mad_power, 2),
            `Max $|\\Delta|$` = fmt(max_power, 2), `$\\rho$ WAB` = fmt(rho_wab, 3),
            `Max rank $\\Delta$ (top 25)` = max_rank, `Top-12 changes` = fmt(top12, 0)) |>
  ktab(align = "llrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-supp-perturb
#| fig-cap: "Change in each FBS team's power rating relative to the baseline prior, by alternative prior. Each point is a team; the box spans the middle half. The week-1 ratings depend on the prior by design, the final ratings hardly at all."
#| fig-scap: "Change in power ratings under alternative priors"
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-asp: 0.45
ps_rat |>
  filter(scenario != "Baseline", tier == 1) |>
  inner_join(base, by = c("fit", "team_id")) |>
  mutate(delta = power - power0, scenario = factor(scenario, levels = sc_levels),
         fit = factor(fit_lab[fit], levels = fit_lab)) |>
  ggplot(aes(scenario, delta)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = col_faint) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4, colour = col_ref) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, colour = col_power, width = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~fit) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Change in power rating (points)")
```

```{r}
pf <- perturb_out |> filter(fit == "final")
p1 <- perturb_out |> filter(fit == "first")
```

At the end of the season the prior is immaterial to what is published: under every alternative the FBS power ratings correlate with the baseline at $\rho `r if (min(pf$rho_power) >= 0.9995) "> 0.999" else paste("\\ge", fmt(min(pf$rho_power), 3))`$, no team's rating moves by more than `r fmt(max(pf$max_power), 1)` points (mean `r fmt(max(pf$mad_power), 2)`), and `r if (max(pf$top12) == 0) "the resume top 12 is unchanged" else paste0("at most ", fmt(max(pf$top12), 0), " team(s) enter or leave the resume top 12")`. More strikingly, the week-1 ratings are also robust, although several structural posteriors there stay close to their priors (@sec-supp-prior): widening every prior fivefold moves no FBS rating by more than `r fmt(p1$max_power[p1$scenario == "SD x 5"], 1)` points, shifting every prior mean by one prior standard deviation moves none by more than `r fmt(max(p1$max_power[grepl("Means", p1$scenario)]), 1)`, and the ratings keep their order ($\rho \ge `r fmt(min(p1$rho_power), 3)`$). The reason is that a week-1 rating rests mainly on the carry-over $\beta d_i$ from last season's final ratings, and $\beta$ is estimated from the week-1 games together with last season's ratings, whatever its prior; the priors on the scales and offsets change how much each team is shrunk towards its conference, which moves ratings by a point or two, not their order. The structural priors therefore stabilise the sampler in data-poor weeks (@sec-priors) without determining what is published. The priors on lower-division offsets and spreads, which the diagnostics flag most, affect FBS ratings only through the handful of cross-tier games.

# Appendix: Reproducibility {#sec-repro .appendix}

The pipeline is run with `targets::tar_make()` from the project root, after setting an API key for CollegeFootballData.com; the first full build fits all `r n_snap` weekly posteriors and takes a few hours on eight cores, and later runs fit only new weeks. `Rscript check_build.R` then verifies the store. This document reads every number and figure from the store at render time and does not refit anything; it is rendered with `quarto render paper/cfb-paper.qmd`. The prior-tuning and half-life experiments are in `analysis/tune_priors.R`, with results in `analysis/*.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-software
#| tbl-cap: "Software versions used for this render."
pk <- c("targets", "cmdstanr", "posterior", "loo", "priorsense", "dplyr", "ggplot2")
tibble::tibble(
  Component = c("R", "CmdStan", pk),
  Version = c(paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
              tryCatch(as.character(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()), error = \(e) "--"),
              map_chr(pk, \(p) tryCatch(as.character(packageVersion(p)), error = \(e) "--")))
) |>
  ktab(align = "ll")
```
